`SticsREval` evaluates a candidate version of the STICS crop model and
compares it to a reference version. This vignette walks through the full
workflow, from a raw SMS repository to a browsable HTML dashboard.

The code below is not run when the vignette is built: it requires a STICS
executable, an SMS repository and the [Quarto CLI](https://quarto.org).

```{r}
library(SticsREval)
```

## Overview

The workflow has three stages, each handled by plain functions taking
explicit arguments:

1. **Prepare the data**: build a STICS text workspace from the SMS
   repository with `gen_workspace_from_sms()`, then run each STICS version on
   it with `run_simulations()`. This produces RDS files of simulations and
   observations.
2. **Evaluate**: compare the candidate version against the observations and
   the reference version with `evaluate()`, and check water and nitrogen
   balances with `balance_closure_test()`.
3. **Report**: render the exported results as an HTML dashboard with
   `render_report()`.

`evaluate()` and `balance_closure_test()` never run STICS themselves: they
only read the RDS files produced by `run_simulations()`. Simulations can thus
be computed once and evaluated many times.

## 1. Prepare the data

### Build the workspace

`gen_workspace_from_sms()` converts the SMS repository (XML input files) into
a STICS text workspace, with one folder per USM:

```{r}
gen_workspace_from_sms(
  sms_path   = "/path/to/sms_repository",
  stics_path = "/path/to/stics_distribution",
  output_dir = "workspace/"
)
```

To restrict the workspace to some USMs, pass their names to `usms`. They can
be read from text files listing one USM per line with `read_usms_files()`:

```{r}
usms <- read_usms_files(c("usms_wheat.txt", "usms_maize.txt"))

gen_workspace_from_sms(
  sms_path   = "/path/to/sms_repository",
  stics_path = "/path/to/stics_distribution",
  output_dir = "workspace/",
  usms       = usms
)
```

### Build the workspace from IDEStics

`gen_workspace_from_idestics()` builds the same kind of workspace from data
retrieved from the IDEStics API. The USMs to generate must be given, and the
rotations they belong to are written to `rotations.csv` in `output_dir`:

```{r}
gen_workspace_from_idestics(
  idestics_url = "https://idestics.example.org",
  stics_path   = "/path/to/stics_distribution",
  output_dir   = "workspace/",
  usms         = usms
)
```

The IDEStics username and password are read from the `IDESTICS_USERNAME` and
`IDESTICS_PASSWORD` environment variables if they are set, for instance in
your user-level `~/.Renviron`. Otherwise, they are prompted for in an
interactive session.

### Run the simulations

Run the reference version once. `run_simulations()` writes
`simulations.rds` and `observations.rds` to `output_dir`:

```{r}
run_simulations(
  stics_exe      = "/path/to/stics_reference",
  usms_workspace = "workspace/",
  metadata_file  = "metadata.csv",
  output_dir     = "reference/"
)
```

By default, the simulated variables are the observed ones. The balance
closure test needs additional, non-observed variables: use
`get_var_from_obs()` to combine both sets into a single run of the candidate
version.

```{r}
balance_vars <- c(
  "init_H2O_balance", "final_H2O_balance",
  "init_plant_N_balance", "final_plant_N_balance",
  "init_soil_mineral_N_balance", "final_soil_mineral_N_balance",
  "init_soil_organic_N_balance", "final_soil_organic_N_balance",
  "init_soil_organic_C_balance", "final_soil_organic_C_balance"
)

obs <- SticsRFiles::get_obs("workspace/")
vars <- c(get_var_from_obs(obs), balance_vars)

run_simulations(
  stics_exe      = "/path/to/stics_candidate",
  usms_workspace = "workspace/",
  metadata_file  = "metadata.csv",
  output_dir     = "outputs/",
  vars           = vars
)
```

## 2. Evaluate

### Statistical evaluation

`evaluate()` runs three evaluations of the candidate version:

- **global**: statistics over all species and USMs combined;
- **per species**: variables whose rRMSE deteriorates by more than
  `percentage` % compared to the reference are flagged;
- **per USM**: USMs where one or more variables are locally degraded compared
  to the reference are flagged.

```{r}
evaluate(
  usms_workspace = "workspace/",
  sim_rds        = "outputs/simulations.rds",
  obs_rds        = "outputs/observations.rds",
  ref_sim_rds    = "reference/simulations.rds",
  output_dir     = "outputs/",
  percentage     = 5
)
```

Results (CSV files, and RDS files with the data of the degraded variables) are written to
`output_dir`, and a summary is printed to the console. Without
`ref_sim_rds`, the candidate version is evaluated against observations only.
Set `stop_on_failure = TRUE` to make `evaluate()` throw an error when an
evaluation fails, e.g. in a CI pipeline.

#### Evaluation criteria

In the global and per-species evaluations, each variable gets a status from
the ratio (in %) of the rRMSE increase of the candidate version over the
reference version:

| Status     | Condition                          |
|------------|------------------------------------|
| Critical   | ratio ≥ `percentage` %             |
| Warning    | 0 % < ratio < `percentage` %       |
| Improved   | ratio ≤ 0 %                        |
| Not tested | fewer than 10 observations         |

An evaluation fails if at least one variable is critical.

In the per-USM evaluation, the following ratio is computed for each variable
and USM:

$$
\text{ratio} = 100 \times \frac{RMSE_{eval} - RMSE_{ref}}{RMSE_{species}}
$$

where $RMSE_{eval}$ and $RMSE_{ref}$ are the RMSE of the candidate and
reference versions on this USM, and $RMSE_{species}$ is the RMSE of the
candidate version over the whole species. A USM fails if one variable has a
ratio above `ratio_threshold` (default 50 %), or if more than
`max_degraded_vars` (default 3) variables have a ratio above
`degraded_threshold` (default 20 %).

The per-USM evaluation has no minimum number of observations: a variable is
tested on a USM even with a single observation there. The only restriction
comes from the species level: a variable that is not tested for a species
(fewer than 10 observations over the whole species) is not tested on any USM
of that species either.

### Balance closure test

`balance_closure_test()` checks, for each USM, that the initial and final
values of the water, plant nitrogen, soil mineral nitrogen, soil organic
nitrogen and soil organic carbon balances differ by at most 1. It stops with
an error listing the USMs where they do not:

```{r}
balance_closure_test(
  sim_rds    = "outputs/simulations.rds",
  output_dir = "outputs/"
)
```

## 3. Report

`render_report()` turns the files written by `evaluate()` into an HTML site,
with a summary homepage, a global page and one page per species:

```{r}
render_report("outputs/")
```

It can also be triggered directly with `evaluate(..., report = TRUE)`. The
site links to its shared assets through relative paths, so keep it intact
when moving or sharing it.

To use the rRMSE comparison plot outside the report, build it from the
exported CSV files with `plot_rrmse_comparison()`:

```{r}
comparison <- read.csv("outputs/csv/global_rrmse_comparison.csv")
plot_rrmse_comparison(comparison, percentage = 5)
```

## Parallel execution

All workflow functions accept `parallel` and `cores` arguments:

```{r}
evaluate(
  usms_workspace = "workspace/",
  sim_rds        = "outputs/simulations.rds",
  obs_rds        = "outputs/observations.rds",
  ref_sim_rds    = "reference/simulations.rds",
  output_dir     = "outputs/",
  parallel       = TRUE,
  cores          = 4
)
```
